correctness.rationale: The affine branches map onto unions of complete levels. Conditional uniformity on the current level is preserved under every finite admissible itinerary. Core levels 1–3 have combined unnormalized mass 1−λ³ and exit probability λ⁴; level 4 has mass λ³(1−λ) and exit probability λ³. Normalizing gives exactly A. Upon exit the height is 1+Geom(1−λ); outside the core the independent increments are Geom(1−λ)−1, with the geometric variable supported on the nonnegative integers. One-level passage has defective PGF r=z(1−λ)/(1−λr), taking the root vanishing at zero. Mixing the geometric entrance height and charging one departure iterate yields H=z(1−A)+Ar²=(1−A/λ)z+(A/λ)r. At z=1 the two regimes are given by r(1)=min(1,(1−λ)/λ); differentiation gives the mean below criticality, and the square-root singularity gives infinite mean at equality. At criticality the survival generating series of the one-level descent is (1−z)^(-1/2), with the core factor A/λ=2/15 for n≥1. As an independent crossover check, group the +1 steps of a Bernoulli walk with up probability p=λ into runs before each −1. The one-level passage exceeds n downward steps exactly when that walk has not hit −1 by time 2n−1. Reflection with the weight (1−p)/p gives its survival as P(S=1)+(1−(1−p)/p)P(S≥3), with S the position at time 2n−1. At p=1/2+u/(2√n), the local binomial limit gives √n P(S=1)→e^(−u²)/√π, while P(S≥3)→Φ(√2u) and the scaled multiplier tends to 2u, including negative u and u=0. This yields the frozen profile after multiplying by A/λ. The checked claims concern only the stated initial law and auxiliary iterates. Reviewed the branch-intersection verifier as finite evidence; did not execute it.

value.rationale: The return observable is natural for the transition from a finite exceptional core to the homogeneous tail. A sharp initial-law normalization and one profile across the recurrent and defective sides give useful quantitative information beyond the qualitative phase transition or a finite computation. This assesses the mathematical contribution of such a law; the complete overlap means it does not warrant a separate accepted finding.
